items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: when he took me out to the Newport Jazz Festival, Melba arranged some things. He said, 'Those arrangements were really good.' She said, 'I didn't do them. That was Lou's arrangement.'

ctx.x: How did Father Crowley convince you to go back to playing?

Father Crowley and Father O'Connor talked to me, several priests. They also asked me to write a Mass, but Father Woods is the only one that really stuck with me until I really began praying, and Dizzy. Dizzy would send Melba, "Go up there and see what Lou's doing. See how she's playing." Melba, I understand, would go back and say, "Man, Lou played some chords and you ought to hear them. They're really great." He said, "Well, get her out."
